questions.question: An agent must be able to look up orders and issue refunds, and nothing else. Which control enforces this?

options.text: An allowed tools list containing only those two tools
options.why: Correct. The agent cannot call tools that are not on the list.

options.text: A sentence in the system prompt
options.why: A prompt can be overridden by a clever message.
Temperature does not restrict tools.
Context size does not restrict tools.

questions.explanation: Platform controls enforce limits that prompts cannot.

questions.question: A refund tool must run only after a person confirms it. What should you configure?

options.why: Correct. The run pauses until a human approves or rejects the call.
This removes evidence and does not add approval.
This is unrelated to approvals.
Caching does not add approval.

questions.scenario: A hosted agent was tricked by a web page into sending data to an unknown website.
questions.question: Which control directly limits where the agent can connect?

options.why: Correct. They restrict which hosts the agent can reach.
This does not limit connections.
This affects capacity.

questions.question: Why should an agent have its own Microsoft Entra identity?

options.why: Identity does not replace guardrails.

options.text: So its access can be granted, audited and revoked separately
options.why: Correct. This supports least privilege and accountability.

questions.question: Which tool design is best for an agent that needs to read one customer order record?

options.text: A tool that fetches any URL
options.why: This gives broad network access.

options.text: A narrow lookup_order tool with a read-only role
options.why: Correct. A narrow tool with limited access follows least privilege.

options.text: A tool that runs any SQL query
options.why: This gives broad access.

options.text: A tool that uses an administrator account
options.why: This exceeds what the task needs.

questions.explanation: Prefer narrow tools over general ones.
